column1: # Which tests a changed path needs. ci/jobs/rust-scope.sh reads this for every file a pull request
# changes outside crates/ (a crate folder maps to its crate and the crates that depend on it) and
# outside the release metadata it places itself (versions, locks, the changelog, memory notes).
# One row per rule: a glob, a tab, and effects separated by spaces. The glob is a shell `case`
# pattern, where `*` also matches `/`. Every rule that matches a path applies, and a path that no
# rule matches runs everything, so a new folder needs a row here (the repo-tests in ci_scope.rs
#   full          the whole workspace, every surface, atl, fuzz and macOS (the test machinery
#   pkg:NAME      the crate NAME changed: it and every crate that depends on it run
#   surface:NAME  replay that golden surface; surface:* replays them all
#   atl           run atl-test (Linux, in the pinned image)
#   atl-macos     run atl-test-macos: atl's own tests on macOS, for a change to atl itself
#   macos         platform-sensitive: run the macOS shards on a pull request (the shims, the
#                 hooks and bin shims, the guard, code that spawns processes, waits or reads the
#                 platform). Push runs always run them.
# --- the test machinery: a change is proved by running everything
# --- atl and the fuzz targets have their own jobs
# --- plugins: the repository checks read every file; some files also feed a golden
# --- the divergence files every golden check reads
# --- everything else: the repository checks (docs, ledger, vendor, evals, workflows, scripts)
# --- platform-sensitive Rust: the guard, code that spawns, waits or reads the platform
